source.text: Ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ἄμπελος ἡ ἀληθινή, καὶ ὁ πατήρ μου ὁ γεωργός ἐστιν·

records.literal_gloss: I am the vine the true, and the Father of me the vinedresser is.

en.L: I am the vine, the true [one], and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father is the vinedresser.
en.B: I am the true vine, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father is the vine grower.
en.R: I am the true vine. My Father is the gardener who takes care of the vine.

es.L: Yo soy la vid, la verdadera, y mi Padre es el labrador.
es.B: Yo soy la vid verdadera, y mi Padre es el viñador.
es.R: Yo soy la vid verdadera. Mi Padre es el que cuida la vid.

fr.L: Je suis la vigne, la vraie, et {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père est le vigneron.
fr.B: Je suis la vraie vigne, et {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père est le vigneron.
fr.R: Je suis la vraie vigne. Mon Père est le vigneron, celui qui prend soin de la vigne.

sw.L: Mimi ni mzabibu, ule wa kweli, na Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} ndiye mtunzaji wa mzabibu.
sw.B: Mimi ni mzabibu wa kweli, na Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} ndiye mkulima wa mizabibu.
sw.R: Mimi ni mzabibu wa kweli. Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} ndiye mtunza bustani anayeutunza mzabibu.

decisions.choice: I am the vine: the last of the sayings in which Jesus says "I am" with a picture
decisions.reason: Here "I am" has a predicate, as in "I am the bread of life" (6:35), "I am the light of the world" (8:12), "I am the gate" (10:7), "I am the good shepherd" (10:11), "I am the resurrection and the life" (11:25) and "I am the way" (14:6). This is the last of these sayings in John. The "I" is stressed: Jesus himself is the vine, and the picture that follows (15:1-8) is about being joined to him.

decisions.choice: the vine: the Scriptures' picture of Israel as the vine God planted
alternatives: a picture drawn only from ordinary farming
decisions.reason: In the Scriptures Israel is God's vine or vineyard, planted and tended by him, which too often bore no good fruit: Psalm 80:9-17; Isaiah 5:1-7; Jeremiah 2:21; Ezekiel 15:1-8; 19:10-14; Hosea 10:1. Psalm 80 links the vine with "the son of man" whom God made strong (80:16, 18). Jesus now says that he is the vine: the people of God are found in him, and fruit comes from being joined to him.

decisions.choice: true: real, the genuine vine to which the picture pointed
alternatives: true as opposed to false or lying
decisions.reason: ἀληθινή means genuine, the real thing, as with the true light (1:9) and the true bread from heaven (6:32). It does not call Israel a false vine; it says that Jesus is the vine in the full sense, the one the old picture was pointing toward. The Greek puts "the true" after "the vine", for weight.

decisions.choice: vinedresser: the one who works the land and tends the vine
decisions.reason: γεωργός is a general word for a farmer, one who works the soil; in the picture of a vine it means the one who plants, cares for and prunes it. The Father is the one who acts on the branches in 15:2. In Isaiah 5:1-7 it is God who planted and tended his vineyard.

decisions.choice: vinedresser (L); vine grower (B); the gardener who takes care of the vine (R)
decisions.reason: Literal uses the traditional word for one who tends vines. Balanced says "vine grower", a plain modern term that keeps the link with the vine. Readable uses the common word "gardener" and says what he does, which also prepares for the pruning in 15:2 (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}
decisions.reason: Every pronoun for Jesus or for God uses the deity_pronoun setting, including "me" and "my" when Jesus speaks of himself, and "he" and "his" for the Father. At the start of a sentence "My" or "He" is written plain. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: labrador (L); viñador (B); el que cuida la vid (R)
decisions.reason: The one who works the land and tends the vine (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: speech tenses: present, passé composé and future as in the Greek, at every level
alternatives: passé simple for the past tenses of speech
decisions.reason: This passage (15:1-11) is all Jesus's speech, so it has no narrative tense to settle; inside speech every level uses the passé composé for the past ("je vous ai dit", "je vous ai aimés"), as people speak and as the rest of John's French does (see 1:19). Where the Greek uses a past form for what happens without fail (verses 6 and 8), French uses the present, as the English does.

decisions.choice: la vigne; le vigneron; les sarments (L, B)
decisions.reason: The terms for the whole of 15:1-8. "Vigne" names the whole plant, as the Greek word does, and is the word of the Scriptures' picture of Israel as God's vine (meaning decision m2); "cep", the traditional rendering, is the woody stock and is unfamiliar to many readers. "Vigneron" is the ordinary word for the one who tends vines (m4), plain enough for every level. Literal keeps the Greek order, "la vigne, la vraie", which gives "true" its weight (m3).

decisions.choice: mzabibu; mtunzaji wa mzabibu (L), mkulima wa mizabibu (B), mtunza bustani anayeutunza mzabibu (R)
decisions.reason: "Mzabibu" is the vine. The meaning note describes one who works the land and tends the vine; plain "mkulima" (farmer) loses the vine, so each level names the work, as the English does (vinedresser, vine grower, gardener). "Mimi ni ..." as in the other "I am" sayings with a picture.

source.text: πᾶν κλῆμα ἐν ἐμοὶ μὴ φέρον καρπὸν αἴρει αὐτό, καὶ πᾶν τὸ καρπὸν φέρον καθαίρει αὐτὸ ἵνα καρπὸν πλείονα φέρῃ.

records.literal_gloss: Every branch in me not bearing fruit, he takes away it; and every [one] the fruit bearing, he cleans it, so that fruit more it may bear.

en.L: Every branch in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} not bearing fruit, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} takes it away; and every [one] bearing fruit, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} cleans it, so that it may bear more fruit.
en.B: He takes away any branch in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} that bears no fruit, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} prunes clean every branch that does bear fruit, so that it will bear more fruit.
en.R: If a branch in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} does not bear fruit, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father takes it away. And if a branch does bear fruit, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} trims it and makes it clean, so that it will bear even more fruit.

es.L: Todo sarmiento que en mí no da fruto, lo quita; y todo el que da fruto, lo limpia, para que dé más fruto.
es.B: Él quita todo sarmiento que en mí no da fruto, y poda y limpia todo el que da fruto, para que dé más fruto todavía.
es.R: Si una rama que está en mí no da fruto, mi Padre la quita. Y si una rama da fruto, la poda y la limpia, para que dé todavía más fruto.

fr.L: Tout sarment en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qui ne porte pas de fruit, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’enlève ; et tout [sarment] qui porte du fruit, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} le purifie, afin qu’il porte plus de fruit.
fr.B: Il enlève tout sarment qui, en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, ne porte pas de fruit, et tout sarment qui porte du fruit, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} le taille pour le rendre pur, afin qu’il en porte davantage.
fr.R: Si une branche qui est en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ne porte pas de fruit, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père l’enlève. Et si une branche porte du fruit, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} la taille pour la rendre pure, afin qu’elle porte encore plus de fruit.

sw.L: Kila tawi ndani {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} lisilozaa matunda, analiondoa; na kila [tawi] linalozaa matunda, analisafisha, ili lizae matunda zaidi.
sw.B: Yeye huliondoa kila tawi ndani {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} lisilozaa matunda, na kila tawi linalozaa matunda hulipogoa likawa safi, ili lizae matunda zaidi.
sw.R: Tawi lililo ndani {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} lisipozaa matunda, Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} huliondoa. Na tawi likizaa matunda, hulipogoa na kulisafisha, ili lizae matunda mengi zaidi.

decisions.choice: takes away: removes the fruitless branch
alternatives: lifts up: raises a branch that trails on the ground so that it can bear fruit
decisions.reason: αἴρει most often means "take away" or "remove" (1:29; 11:39, 48; 17:15; 19:15, 31, 38), and here it stands against pruning the fruitful branch: one kind is removed, the other cleaned. 15:6 goes on to the branch that is thrown out. The verb can also mean "lift up" (5:8-12; 8:59), and some take the picture to be of a vinedresser raising fallen branches off the ground in care for them. The common meaning and the contrast in the verse favor "takes away", but the other reading is possible.

decisions.choice: cleans: prunes, with a play on "clean" in 15:3
alternatives: prunes, with no play on words
decisions.reason: καθαίρει means to clean or cleanse; used of a vine it means to clear away growth so that the branch bears more. Jesus chooses this verb, not the usual word for pruning, and then says in the next breath, "you are clean" (καθαροί, 15:3), a word from the same root. The pruning of the branches and the cleanness of the disciples are one thought.

decisions.choice: fruit: the life that grows from being joined to Jesus
decisions.reason: "Fruit" in the picture is what a branch produces because it is joined to the vine. The passage fills it out: prayer that is answered (15:7), the Father glorified and disciples shown to be his (15:8), love and obedience (15:9-12), and joy (15:11). In 15:16 Jesus speaks of fruit that lasts. It is not named more narrowly than that.

decisions.choice: cleans (L); prunes clean (B); trims it and makes it clean (R)
decisions.reason: Every level keeps the word "clean", so that the reader hears the link with "you are clean" in 15:3 (meaning decision m2). Balanced and Readable add the gardener's word, so that the picture stays clear. "Fruit" is kept at every level: it is the key word of the picture.

decisions.choice: If a branch ...; my Father takes it away
decisions.reason: Readable names the Father as the one who acts, since the subject of the verbs is the vinedresser of 15:1, and breaks the sentence in two.

decisions.choice: limpia (L); poda y limpia (B); la poda y la limpia (R)
decisions.reason: Every level keeps "limpiar", so the play on "limpios" in 15:3 (and 13:10) can be heard (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: sarmiento (L, B); rama (R)
decisions.reason: The branch of a vine. "Pámpano" is the traditional word but few readers now know it. "Él" at the start of the Balanced sentence is written plain.

decisions.choice: le purifie (L); le taille pour le rendre pur (B); la taille pour la rendre pure (R)
decisions.reason: Every level keeps the word "pur" so that the reader hears the link with "vous êtes purs" in 15:3 (meaning decision m2), as the English keeps "clean". "Émonder" is the gardener's word for pruning but loses that link and is rare; "nettoyer" would lead to "vous êtes propres", which sounds like hygiene. Balanced and Readable add "tailler" so that the picture of the vine stays clear. The "il" and "le" that stand for the branch have no setting.

decisions.choice: une branche (R); un sarment (L, B)
decisions.reason: "Sarment" is the exact word for the branch of a vine but is not known to many young readers, so Readable says "branche" throughout 15:2-6, as the English Readable keeps "branch".

decisions.choice: analisafisha (L); hulipogoa likawa safi (B); hulipogoa na kulisafisha (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning note: to prune, with a play on "clean" in verse 3. "Kusafisha" (to make clean) keeps the play with "safi" (clean) in the next verse; Balanced and Readable add "kupogoa" (to prune) so the vine-grower's work is clear, as the English does.

source.text: ἤδη ὑμεῖς καθαροί ἐστε διὰ τὸν λόγον ὃν λελάληκα ὑμῖν·

records.literal_gloss: Already you clean are because of the word that I have spoken to you.

en.L: Already you are clean on account of the word that I have spoken to you.
en.B: Because of the word I have spoken to you, you are clean already.
en.R: The message I have spoken to you has already made you clean.

es.L: Ya {{plural_you:ustedes están limpios|vosotros estáis limpios}} por la palabra que {{plural_you:les|os}} he hablado.
es.B: Por la palabra que {{plural_you:les|os}} he hablado, {{plural_you:ustedes ya están limpios|vosotros ya estáis limpios}}.
es.R: El mensaje que {{plural_you:les|os}} he dado ya {{plural_you:los|os}} ha dejado limpios.

fr.L: Déjà, vous, vous êtes purs à cause de la parole que je vous ai dite.
fr.B: Grâce à la parole que je vous ai dite, vous êtes déjà purs.
fr.R: Le message que je vous ai donné vous a déjà rendus purs.

sw.L: Tayari ninyi ni safi kwa sababu ya neno nililowaambia.
sw.B: Kwa sababu ya neno nililowaambia, ninyi ni safi tayari.

decisions.choice: you are clean: the disciples already belong to Jesus and are cleansed, as in 13:10
decisions.reason: At the foot-washing Jesus said, "you are clean, but not all of you" (13:10-11), and Judas has now gone out (13:30). Speaking to the eleven, he says they are already clean. In the picture they are the fruitful branches that the Father has cleaned (15:2): the cleansing is not still ahead of them.

decisions.choice: because of the word: Jesus's message is the reason they are clean
alternatives: through the word, as the means
decisions.reason: διὰ with this case gives the reason: it is on account of the word that they are clean. The word is Jesus's whole message, which they have received and kept (8:31; 17:6, 8, 17). The perfect "I have spoken" looks back on all he has said and its lasting effect.

decisions.choice: Because of the word ... you are clean already (B); The message ... has already made you clean (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the reason first and keeps "clean" for the link with 15:2. Readable makes the word the subject, "has made you clean", a plain way of saying "because of" (meaning decision m2), and says "message" for the word as Jesus's whole teaching.

decisions.choice: limpios
decisions.reason: The word of 13:10 and of 15:2 (meaning decision m1).

source.text: μείνατε ἐν ἐμοί, κἀγὼ ἐν ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: Remain in me, and I in you.

en.L: Remain in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I in you.
en.B: Remain in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I will remain in you.
en.R: Remain in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I will remain in you.

fr.B: Demeurez en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, et je demeurerai en vous.
fr.R: Demeurez en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, et je demeurerai en vous.

decisions.choice: remain: stay joined to Jesus, a lasting union
decisions.reason: μείνατε is the verb John uses both for staying in a place (1:38-39) and for the lasting union between Jesus and those who are his (6:56; 8:31; 14:10, 17). It appears ten times in 15:4-10, more than anywhere else in the Gospel. The command is not to come to Jesus for the first time, but to stay where they already are, joined to him.

decisions.choice: and I in you: a promise that goes with the command: remain in me, and I will remain in you
alternatives: a comparison: remain in me, as I remain in you
a second part of the command: and see that I remain in you
decisions.reason: The Greek has no verb in the second half, so it must be supplied. Most naturally it is a promise joined to the command: if they remain in him, he will remain in them (compare 6:56; 14:20, 23). It can also be read as a comparison, "as I remain in you", or as part of the command, that they let him remain in them. The two-way union is clear on every reading; the text does not settle which link between the halves is meant.

decisions.choice: and I will remain in you
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply the verb as a promise (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps the short Greek form.

decisions.choice: remain, at every level
decisions.reason: John's word is "remain" every time it occurs in 15:4-10, at every level, so that a reader can see one verb carrying the whole passage. "Abide" is the traditional word but is no longer everyday English. "Stay joined" or "live in" would explain the picture but hide the repeated word.

decisions.choice: permanecer, at every level
decisions.reason: The book-wide verb for the weighty sense of remaining, used for every occurrence in 15:1-10 (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: y yo permaneceré en ustedes
decisions.reason: As in English: a promise that goes with the command (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: demeurer, at every level, in each of its uses in 15:4-10
decisions.reason: One verb carries the whole passage (meaning decision m1), and the English keeps "remain" at every level so that readers can see it. French "demeurer" is the book-wide word for this sense (see 1:38-39 and 14:10) and is understood by young readers in this phrase, so Readable keeps it too. "Rester" is plainer but would also be used for ordinary staying and would hide the link. Literal uses the stressed "moi" in the verbless clause, with the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: kukaa, at every level
decisions.reason: "Kukaa" for this verb throughout John, so that "remain" stays one word for the reader through the vine passage (verses 4-10, 16), as the English keeps "remain".

source.text: καθὼς τὸ κλῆμα οὐ δύναται καρπὸν φέρειν ἀφ’ ἑαυτοῦ ἐὰν μὴ μένῃ ἐν τῇ ἀμπέλῳ, οὕτως οὐδὲ ὑμεῖς ἐὰν μὴ ἐν ἐμοὶ μένητε.

records.literal_gloss: Just as the branch not is able fruit to bear from itself unless it remains in the vine, so neither you unless in me you remain.

en.L: Just as the branch is not able to bear fruit from itself unless it remains in the vine, so neither [can] you unless you remain in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: A branch cannot bear fruit by itself; it must remain in the vine. In the same way, you cannot bear fruit unless you remain in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: A branch cannot produce fruit on its own. It has to remain in the vine. In the same way, you cannot produce fruit unless you remain in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: Así como el sarmiento no puede dar fruto por sí mismo si no permanece en la vid, así tampoco {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, si no {{plural_you:permanecen|permanecéis}} en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.B: El sarmiento no puede dar fruto por sí mismo; tiene que permanecer en la vid. Del mismo modo, {{plural_you:ustedes no pueden|vosotros no podéis}} dar fruto si no {{plural_you:permanecen|permanecéis}} en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.R: Una rama no puede dar fruto por su cuenta. Tiene que permanecer en la vid. Del mismo modo, {{plural_you:ustedes no pueden|vosotros no podéis}} dar fruto si no {{plural_you:permanecen|permanecéis}} en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.

fr.L: Comme le sarment ne peut pas porter de fruit de lui-même s’il ne demeure pas dans la vigne, ainsi [vous ne le pouvez] pas non plus, si vous ne demeurez pas en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.B: Un sarment ne peut pas porter de fruit par lui-même ; il doit demeurer dans la vigne. De la même manière, vous ne pouvez pas porter de fruit si vous ne demeurez pas en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.R: Une branche ne peut pas produire de fruit toute seule. Elle doit demeurer dans la vigne. De la même façon, vous ne pouvez pas produire de fruit si vous ne demeurez pas en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.

sw.L: Kama vile tawi haliwezi kuzaa matunda lenyewe lisipokaa katika mzabibu, vivyo hivyo ninyi pia [hamwezi] msipokaa ndani {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.
sw.B: Tawi haliwezi kuzaa matunda peke yake; ni lazima likae katika mzabibu. Vivyo hivyo, ninyi hamwezi kuzaa matunda msipokaa ndani {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.
sw.R: Tawi haliwezi kutoa matunda lenyewe. Ni lazima likae katika mzabibu. Vivyo hivyo, ninyi hamwezi kutoa matunda msipokaa ndani {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.

decisions.choice: just as ... so neither: the branch and the disciples are compared point for point
decisions.reason: καθὼς sets up the picture and οὕτως applies it. The second half leaves the verb to be supplied from the first: neither can you bear fruit. Both halves end with the same condition, "unless ... remains/remain", so the two uses of the verb stand side by side.

decisions.choice: from itself: by its own power, cut off from its source
decisions.reason: The branch has no life of its own; whatever fruit it bears comes from the vine. Jesus says the same of himself and the Father: the Son can do nothing from himself (5:19, 30). The same phrase returns in 15:5 in another form: "apart from me".

decisions.choice: remains in the vine: joined to the vine, taking its life from it
decisions.reason: In the picture "remain" means stay attached to the vine; for the disciples it means stay joined to Jesus, keeping his words and remaining in his love (15:7, 9-10). The word that once described the first disciples staying where Jesus was (1:39) here describes a life lived in him.

decisions.choice: you cannot bear fruit (B); you cannot produce fruit (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply the verb the Greek leaves understood (meaning decision m1) and break the long sentence. Readable says "produce fruit" and "on its own", plain words for the same picture; "fruit" and "remain" stay at every level.

decisions.choice: no pueden dar fruto
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m1). "Sí mismo" is the branch and takes no setting.

source.text: ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ἄμπελος, ὑμεῖς τὰ κλήματα.

records.literal_gloss: I am the vine, you the branches.

en.L: I am the vine, you [are] the branches.
en.B: I am the vine; you are the branches.
en.R: I am the vine, and you are the branches.

es.L: Yo soy la vid, {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} los sarmientos.
es.B: Yo soy la vid; {{plural_you:ustedes son|vosotros sois}} los sarmientos.
es.R: Yo soy la vid, y {{plural_you:ustedes son|vosotros sois}} las ramas.

fr.L: Je suis la vigne, vous [êtes] les sarments.
fr.B: Je suis la vigne ; vous êtes les sarments.
fr.R: Je suis la vigne, et vous êtes les branches.

sw.B: Mimi ni mzabibu; ninyi ni matawi.
sw.R: Mimi ni mzabibu, nanyi ni matawi.

decisions.choice: I am the vine, you the branches: Jesus repeats the picture and now names the disciples' place in it
decisions.reason: 15:1 named the vine and the vinedresser; here Jesus says plainly who the branches are. The Greek sets "I" and "you" side by side and leaves out the second verb. Every branch in the picture is "in me" (15:2): the branches belong to the vine and have no life apart from it.

decisions.choice: [are]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the verb the Greek leaves understood; Balanced and Readable supply it without brackets.

decisions.choice: no verb
decisions.reason: Spanish can leave out the verb, as the Greek does, so Literal brackets nothing.

source.text: ὁ μένων ἐν ἐμοὶ κἀγὼ ἐν αὐτῷ οὗτος φέρει καρπὸν πολύν, ὅτι χωρὶς ἐμοῦ οὐ δύνασθε ποιεῖν οὐδέν.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] remaining in me and I in him, this [one] bears fruit much, because apart from me not you are able to do nothing.

en.L: The one who remains in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and I in {{gender:them|him}}, this one bears much fruit, because apart from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} you are able to do nothing.
en.B: Whoever remains in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} remaining in {{gender:them|him}}, is the one who bears much fruit, because you can do nothing apart from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: Those who remain in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I in them, are the ones who bear a lot of fruit. You cannot do anything without {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: El que permanece en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, y yo en {{gender:esa persona|él}}, ese da mucho fruto, porque separados de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} nada {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} hacer.
es.B: El que permanece en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, y yo en {{gender:esa persona|él}}, es el que da mucho fruto, porque separados de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} no {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} hacer nada.
es.R: Los que permanecen en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, y yo en ellos, son los que dan mucho fruto. Sin {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} no {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} hacer nada.

fr.L: {{gender:La personne|Celui}} qui demeure en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} en {{gender:elle|lui}}, {{gender:celle-là|celui-là}} porte beaucoup de fruit, parce qu’en dehors de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} vous ne pouvez rien faire.
fr.B: Si quelqu’un demeure en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et que je demeure en {{gender:cette personne|lui}}, c’est {{gender:elle|lui}} qui porte beaucoup de fruit, car vous ne pouvez rien faire en dehors de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.R: Ceux qui demeurent en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, et {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} en eux, sont ceux qui portent beaucoup de fruit. Sans {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, vous ne pouvez rien faire.

sw.L: Anayekaa ndani {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ndani yake, huyo anazaa matunda mengi, kwa sababu bila {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} hamwezi kufanya chochote.
sw.B: Yeyote anayekaa ndani {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nikikaa ndani yake, ndiye anayezaa matunda mengi, kwa sababu bila {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} hamwezi kufanya kitu.
sw.R: Wale wanaokaa ndani {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} ndani yao, ndio wanaozaa matunda mengi. Hamwezi kufanya lolote bila {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}.

decisions.choice: the one who remains in me ... this one bears much fruit: the one who remains, and no other
decisions.reason: οὗτος ("this one") points back to the one who remains, with emphasis: that person is the one who bears much fruit. The short "and I in him" again leaves the verb understood (15:4): Jesus remains in the one who remains in him (6:56).

decisions.choice: apart from me you can do nothing: nothing that is fruit, nothing of lasting worth
decisions.reason: The words belong to the picture: a branch cut off from the vine can bear no fruit at all. Jesus is not saying that people apart from him cannot act, but that the fruit he is speaking of comes only from being joined to him. The Greek has a double negative, "not ... nothing", which strengthens the point. Compare 5:19, 30, where the Son can do nothing from himself apart from the Father.

decisions.choice: because: the reason the one who remains bears much fruit
decisions.reason: ὅτι gives the reason: fruit comes from remaining in him, because without him nothing can come.

decisions.choice: {{gender:them|him}} (L, B); those ... them (R)
decisions.reason: The one who remains in Jesus may be a man or a woman, so the pronoun uses the gender setting. Readable uses the plural, as at 6:56, which needs no span.

decisions.choice: you can do nothing apart from me (B); You cannot do anything without me (R)
alternatives: for apart from me you can do nothing
decisions.reason: Balanced puts "apart from me" at the end, where it falls with weight in English. Readable makes a separate, short sentence, which shows the reason plainly.

decisions.choice: {{gender:esa persona|él}}
decisions.reason: The stressed generic pronoun takes the gender setting; Readable uses the plural, as in English.

decisions.choice: {{gender:La personne|Celui}} ... {{gender:elle|lui}} ... {{gender:celle-là|celui-là}} (L); {{gender:cette personne|lui}} ... {{gender:elle|lui}} (B)
alternatives: Celui qui ... lui ... celui-là, with no setting
decisions.reason: The one who remains in Jesus may be a man or a woman (English rendering decision r-en-1). As in 14:12 and 14:23, the whole chain of words for that person takes the gender setting, so each option reads consistently. Readable uses the plural, as the English does; "eux" is the ordinary plural for men and women together and needs no setting. In "et moi en eux" the stressed "moi" is Jesus and takes the deity_pronoun setting at both levels where it occurs.

decisions.choice: ndani yake, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English needs "them" with "him" as the traditional alternative; Swahili "yake" and the verb prefix "a-" say nothing about sex, so there is no span here or in verses 6 and 13, as at 14:12.

source.text: ἐὰν μή τις μένῃ ἐν ἐμοί, ἐβλήθη ἔξω ὡς τὸ κλῆμα καὶ ἐξηράνθη, καὶ συνάγουσιν αὐτὰ καὶ εἰς τὸ πῦρ βάλλουσιν καὶ καίεται.

records.literal_gloss: If not anyone remains in me, he was thrown outside like the branch and was dried up, and they gather them and into the fire they throw, and it is burned.

en.L: If anyone does not remain in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{gender:they are|he is}} thrown outside like the branch and {{gender:wither|withers}}; and they gather them and throw [them] into the fire, and they are burned.
en.B: Anyone who does not remain in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is thrown out like a branch and dries up. People gather the branches, throw them into the fire, and they burn.
en.R: Anyone who does not remain in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is like a branch that is thrown away and dries up. People pick up dry branches like that and throw them into the fire to be burned.

es.L: Si alguno no permanece en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, es echado fuera como el sarmiento, y se seca; y los recogen y los echan al fuego, y arden.
es.B: El que no permanece en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} es echado fuera como un sarmiento y se seca. La gente recoge los sarmientos, los echa al fuego, y arden.
es.R: El que no permanece en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} es como una rama que se tira y se seca. La gente recoge las ramas secas y las echa al fuego para quemarlas.

fr.L: Si quelqu’un ne demeure pas en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, {{gender:cette personne est jetée|il est jeté}} dehors comme le sarment et se dessèche ; et on les ramasse et on [les] jette au feu, et ils brûlent.
fr.B: Celui qui ne demeure pas en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} est jeté dehors comme un sarment, et se dessèche. On ramasse les sarments, on les jette au feu, et ils brûlent.
fr.R: Celui qui ne demeure pas en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} est comme une branche qu’on jette et qui se dessèche. On ramasse ces branches sèches et on les jette au feu pour les brûler.

sw.L: Mtu yeyote asipokaa ndani {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, ametupwa nje kama tawi na amenyauka; nao huyakusanya na kuyatupa motoni, nayo yanaungua.
sw.B: Yeyote asiyekaa ndani {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} anatupwa nje kama tawi na kukauka. Watu huyakusanya matawi hayo, huyatupa motoni, nayo huungua.
sw.R: Yeyote asiyekaa ndani {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} ni kama tawi linalotupwa nje na kukauka. Watu huokota matawi makavu kama hayo na kuyatupa motoni yaungue.

decisions.choice: is thrown out ... withers: past-tense verbs for what happens without fail
alternatives: was thrown out ... withered, of something already past
decisions.reason: ἐβλήθη and ἐξηράνθη are past (aorist) forms, but they follow "if anyone does not remain" and describe what happens in that case. Greek can use this form for a result that follows as surely as if it had already happened, as in a proverb. The verbs that follow ("they gather ... throw ... it is burned") are present. So the sense is a sure and immediate result, not a story about the past.

decisions.choice: they gather them: "they" is general, the people who clear dead branches in the picture
decisions.reason: The plural "they" has no stated subject; it is a general "they", meaning whoever gathers dead wood. "Them" is plural: the dried-up branches as a group, though the sentence began with "anyone" in the singular. The picture does not name who the gatherers stand for.

decisions.choice: the fire: a picture of judgment on the one who does not remain in Jesus
alternatives: the loss only of reward or usefulness
a statement of who can or cannot finally fall away
decisions.reason: A branch cut off from the vine is good only for burning, and Ezekiel 15:2-7 uses this very picture of judgment on the people of Jerusalem; compare also Matthew 3:10 and 7:19. Jesus states what the picture says: separation from him means withering and the fire. The verse does not say who in the end does not remain, and it does not by itself settle the long debate about whether a true believer can fall away. Some read it of those who never truly belonged, like Judas (13:10-11, 30; 17:12; 1 John 2:19); others read it as a real warning to disciples. The text holds out the warning without settling that question.

decisions.choice: {{gender:they are|he is}} ... {{gender:wither|withers}}
decisions.reason: "Anyone" may be a man or a woman, so the pronoun and its verb use the gender setting. Balanced and Readable say "anyone who" and need no pronoun.

decisions.choice: People gather the branches (B); People pick up dry branches like that (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the general "they" as "people" and say "branches" for "them", so that no reader takes "they" to mean a group already named (meaning decision m2). Readable says "is like a branch" so that the picture is plainly a comparison.

decisions.choice: no gender setting
decisions.reason: Spanish needs no pronoun for "he is thrown out ... withers".

decisions.choice: La gente recoge los sarmientos (B) / las ramas secas (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: "they" is general (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: {{gender:cette personne est jetée|il est jeté}} (L); no pronoun (B, R)
alternatives: il est jeté, with no setting
decisions.reason: "Anyone" may be a man or a woman (English rendering decision r-en-1). Literal needs a pronoun, which takes the gender setting together with the participle that agrees with it; the verb "se dessèche" is the same for both and stays outside the span. Balanced and Readable say "celui qui" and let the verbs share that subject, so they need no pronoun. "On" is the French general "they" (meaning decision m2).

source.text: ἐὰν μείνητε ἐν ἐμοὶ καὶ τὰ ῥήματά μου ἐν ὑμῖν μείνῃ, ὃ ἐὰν θέλητε αἰτήσασθε καὶ γενήσεται ὑμῖν·

records.literal_gloss: If you remain in me and the words of me in you remain, whatever if you wish ask, and it will come to be for you.

en.L: If you remain in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words remain in you, ask whatever you wish, and it will come to be for you.
en.B: If you remain in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words remain in you, ask for whatever you want, and it will be done for you.
en.R: If you remain in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words remain in you, you can ask for anything you want, and it will be done for you.

es.L: Si {{plural_you:permanecen|permanecéis}} en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, y mis palabras permanecen en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, {{plural_you:pidan|pedid}} lo que {{plural_you:quieran|queráis}}, y se {{plural_you:les|os}} hará.
es.B: Si {{plural_you:permanecen|permanecéis}} en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} y mis palabras permanecen en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, {{plural_you:pidan|pedid}} lo que {{plural_you:quieran|queráis}}, y se {{plural_you:les|os}} concederá.
es.R: Si {{plural_you:permanecen|permanecéis}} en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} y mis palabras permanecen en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} pedir lo que {{plural_you:quieran|queráis}}, y se {{plural_you:les|os}} concederá.

fr.L: Si vous demeurez en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et que {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} paroles demeurent en vous, demandez ce que vous voulez, et cela se fera pour vous.
fr.B: Si vous demeurez en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et si {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} paroles demeurent en vous, demandez tout ce que vous désirez, et cela se réalisera pour vous.
fr.R: Si vous demeurez en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et si {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} paroles demeurent en vous, vous pouvez demander tout ce que vous voulez, et vous le recevrez.

sw.L: Ikiwa mnakaa ndani {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} yanakaa ndani yenu, ombeni chochote mnachotaka, nacho kitatokea kwenu.
sw.B: Mkikaa ndani {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} yakakaa ndani yenu, ombeni chochote mnachotaka, nanyi mtafanyiwa.
sw.R: Mkikaa ndani {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} yakakaa ndani yenu, mnaweza kuomba chochote mnachotaka, nanyi mtafanyiwa.

decisions.choice: ask (a command), as the SBLGNT reads
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads αἰτήσασθε, a command: "ask". Many manuscripts read a future form that differs by one letter, "you will ask". Either way, asking and receiving are promised to those who remain in Jesus. A reviewer should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: whatever you wish: asking shaped by Jesus's words that remain in them
alternatives: an unlimited promise apart from the condition
decisions.reason: The promise follows two conditions: that they remain in Jesus and that his words remain in them. Those whose wishes are shaped by his words ask for what bears fruit (15:8, 16). Compare 14:13-14, asking in his name, and 1 John 5:14, asking according to his will.

decisions.choice: my words: Jesus's sayings, his teaching in its parts
decisions.reason: ῥήματά is the plural of the word for something spoken. It means the same teaching as "the word" in 15:3, seen in its many sayings (compare 14:23-24). Here Jesus's words, too, are said to "remain" in the disciples.

decisions.choice: it will be done for you (B, R); you can ask (R)
decisions.reason: "Will come to be for you" means that what they ask will happen; Balanced and Readable say "will be done for you". Readable softens the command to "you can ask", which keeps the invitation in plain words.

decisions.choice: se les concederá (B, R); pueden pedir (R)
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m2).

source.text: ἐν τούτῳ ἐδοξάσθη ὁ πατήρ μου ἵνα καρπὸν πολὺν φέρητε καὶ γένησθε ἐμοὶ μαθηταί.

records.literal_gloss: In this was glorified the Father of me, that fruit much you bear and become my disciples.

en.L: In this {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father is glorified, that you bear much fruit and become {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} disciples.
en.B: This is how {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father is glorified: that you bear much fruit and so prove to be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} disciples.
en.R: When you bear a lot of fruit, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father is glorified, and you show that you are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} disciples.

es.L: En esto es glorificado mi Padre: en que {{plural_you:den|deis}} mucho fruto y {{plural_you:lleguen|lleguéis}} a ser mis discípulos.
es.B: Así es glorificado mi Padre: en que {{plural_you:den|deis}} mucho fruto y {{plural_you:demuestren|demostréis}} así que {{plural_you:son|sois}} mis discípulos.
es.R: Cuando {{plural_you:dan|dais}} mucho fruto, mi Padre es glorificado, y {{plural_you:ustedes muestran|vosotros mostráis}} que {{plural_you:son|sois}} mis discípulos.

fr.L: En ceci {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père est glorifié : que vous portiez beaucoup de fruit et deveniez {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} disciples.
fr.B: C’est en ceci que {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père est glorifié : que vous portiez beaucoup de fruit, et que vous vous montriez ainsi {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} disciples.
fr.R: Quand vous portez beaucoup de fruit, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père est glorifié, et vous montrez que vous êtes {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} disciples.

sw.L: Katika hili Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} ametukuzwa, kwamba mzae matunda mengi na mwe wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}.
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} anavyotukuzwa: mzae matunda mengi, na hivyo mthibitike kuwa wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}.
sw.R: Mnapozaa matunda mengi, Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} anatukuzwa, nanyi mnaonyesha kwamba ni wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}.

decisions.choice: and become (part of the same purpose), as the SBLGNT reads
alternatives: and you will be my disciples (a separate result)
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads γένησθε, a form that goes with "that you bear": the Father is glorified in this, that you bear much fruit and become disciples. Many manuscripts have a future, "and you will be my disciples", a separate result that follows. The two forms differ by a letter or two. The sense is close either way. A reviewer should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: in this ... that: "this" points forward to bearing much fruit
alternatives: "this" points back to the answered prayer of 15:7
decisions.reason: ἐν τούτῳ looks ahead to the clause that follows: the Father is glorified in the disciples' bearing much fruit. It may also gather up 15:7, since answered prayer is part of that fruit (14:13: the Father is glorified in the Son when he does what they ask).

decisions.choice: is glorified: a past-tense form for what is sure and complete
alternatives: was glorified, at some past time
decisions.reason: ἐδοξάσθη is an aorist, a past form, but it speaks of what happens whenever the disciples bear fruit. As in 13:31, John uses this form for glory that is certain, seen as already done.

decisions.choice: become my disciples: show themselves to be disciples, grow into what they already are
alternatives: become disciples for the first time
decisions.reason: They are already his disciples (13:35; 15:3). To "become" disciples is to be shown as true disciples by what they bear, as 8:31 says: "if you remain in my word, you really are my disciples".

decisions.choice: so prove to be (B); show that you are (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "become". Balanced and Readable say what the word means here (meaning decision m4), since "become my disciples" could suggest they were not disciples before.

decisions.choice: When you bear a lot of fruit, my Father is glorified
decisions.reason: Readable puts the condition first and drops the pointer word "this" (meaning decision m2). "Glorified" and "fruit" stay.

decisions.choice: demuestren (B); muestran (R)
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m4).

source.text: καθὼς ἠγάπησέν με ὁ πατήρ, κἀγὼ ὑμᾶς ἠγάπησα, μείνατε ἐν τῇ ἀγάπῃ τῇ ἐμῇ.

records.literal_gloss: Just as loved me the Father, I also you loved; remain in the love the mine.

en.L: Just as the Father loved {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, I also loved you; remain in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} love.
en.B: I have loved you just as the Father has loved {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Remain in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} love.
en.R: The Father has loved {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I have loved you in the same way. Remain in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} love.

es.L: Como el Padre me amó, también yo {{plural_you:los|os}} amé; {{plural_you:permanezcan|permaneced}} en mi amor.
es.B: Yo {{plural_you:los|os}} he amado así como el Padre me ha amado a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. {{plural_you:Permanezcan|Permaneced}} en mi amor.
es.R: El Padre me ha amado, y yo {{plural_you:los|os}} he amado a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} de la misma manera. {{plural_you:Permanezcan|Permaneced}} en mi amor.

fr.L: De même que le Père {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a aimé, {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} aussi, je vous ai aimés ; demeurez dans l’amour qui est le {{deity_pronoun:mien|Mien}}.
fr.B: Je vous ai aimés comme le Père {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a aimé. Demeurez dans {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} amour.
fr.R: Le Père {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a aimé, et je vous ai aimés de la même façon. Demeurez dans {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} amour.

sw.L: Kama vile Baba alivyonipenda, {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} pia niliwapenda ninyi; kaeni katika upendo {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}.
sw.B: Nimewapenda kama vile Baba alivyonipenda. Kaeni katika upendo {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}.
sw.R: Baba amenipenda, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nimewapenda ninyi vivyo hivyo. Kaeni katika upendo {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}.

decisions.choice: just as the Father loved me, I also loved you: Jesus's love for them is of the same kind as the Father's love for him
alternatives: the Father's love only as an example
decisions.reason: καθὼς joins the two loves: the Father's love for the Son is both the pattern and the source of the Son's love for the disciples (3:35; 17:23, 26). Both verbs are aorists, past forms that sum up the whole of that love; Jesus's love for them will reach its fullest point in giving his life (13:1; 15:13).

decisions.choice: my love: the love Jesus has for them
decisions.reason: "My love" here is the love Jesus has for them, the love he has just described. To remain in it is to stay within that love and live in it, not to keep up their own love by effort. 15:10 says how they remain in it.

decisions.choice: I have loved you just as the Father has loved me (B); The Father has loved me, and I have loved you in the same way (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "has loved" for the aorist, since the love is still present (meaning decision m1). Balanced puts Jesus's love for them first, and Readable says it in two plain clauses. "Remain" stays at every level.

decisions.choice: Yo los he amado así como el Padre me ha amado (B); El Padre me ha amado, y yo los he amado (R)
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: l’amour qui est le {{deity_pronoun:mien|Mien}}
decisions.reason: The Greek has the fuller form of "my", after the noun with its own article ("the love, the mine"), which stresses that it is Jesus's love for them (meaning decision m2). Literal shows the stress with "qui est le mien"; Balanced and Readable say "mon amour". The passé composé "je vous ai aimés" serves for the Greek past at every level, since French uses it for a love that is still present (m1).

source.text: ἐὰν τὰς ἐντολάς μου τηρήσητε, μενεῖτε ἐν τῇ ἀγάπῃ μου, καθὼς ἐγὼ τὰς ἐντολὰς τοῦ πατρός μου τετήρηκα καὶ μένω αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ ἀγάπῃ.

records.literal_gloss: If the commandments of me you keep, you will remain in the love of me, just as I the commandments of the Father of me have kept and remain of him in the love.

en.L: If you keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments, you will remain in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} love, just as I have kept the commandments of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father and remain in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} love.
en.B: You will remain in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} love if you keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments, just as I have kept the commandments {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and remain in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} love.
en.R: If you obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commands, you will remain in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} love. In the same way, I have obeyed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father's commands, and I remain in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} love.

es.L: Si {{plural_you:guardan|guardáis}} mis mandamientos, {{plural_you:permanecerán|permaneceréis}} en mi amor, así como yo he guardado los mandamientos de mi Padre y permanezco en su amor.
es.B: {{plural_you:Permanecerán|Permaneceréis}} en mi amor si {{plural_you:guardan|guardáis}} mis mandamientos, así como yo he guardado los mandamientos que mi Padre me dio y permanezco en su amor.
es.R: Si {{plural_you:obedecen|obedecéis}} mis mandatos, {{plural_you:permanecerán|permaneceréis}} en mi amor. Del mismo modo, yo he obedecido los mandatos de mi Padre, y permanezco en su amor.

fr.L: Si vous gardez {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} commandements, vous demeurerez dans {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} amour, tout comme {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, j’ai gardé les commandements de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père et je demeure dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} amour.
fr.B: Vous demeurerez dans {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} amour si vous gardez {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} commandements, comme j’ai gardé les commandements que {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a donnés et que je demeure dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} amour.
fr.R: Si vous mettez en pratique {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} commandements, vous demeurerez dans {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} amour. De la même façon, j’ai mis en pratique les commandements de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père, et je demeure dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} amour.

decisions.choice: keeping his commandments is the way the disciples remain in his love
alternatives: obedience as the price of being loved
decisions.reason: Jesus has already loved them (15:9); keeping his commandments does not earn that love but is how they stay in it. The same link runs through 14:15, 21 and 23: love for Jesus shows itself in keeping his commandments. The chief commandment is named in 13:34 and again in 15:12: love one another.

decisions.choice: just as I have kept my Father's commandments: Jesus's own obedience is the pattern
decisions.reason: Jesus remains in the Father's love by doing what the Father commanded him (8:29; 10:18; 12:49-50; 14:31). The perfect "I have kept" sums up his whole life of obedience, while "I remain" is present: the Son goes on remaining in the Father's love. The disciples' life is to have the same shape.

decisions.choice: you will remain ... I remain: the same verb for the disciples and for Jesus
decisions.reason: μενεῖτε is a future, the result promised to those who keep his commandments; μένω is present. The verse uses the passage's key verb twice, once of the disciples in Jesus's love and once of Jesus in the Father's love.

decisions.choice: obey my commands (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "obey" and "commands", plain words for keeping commandments, as it does in 14:15 and 14:21. Literal and Balanced keep "keep" and "commandments".

decisions.choice: You will remain in my love if you keep my commandments; the commandments my Father gave me
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the promise first and says "the commandments my Father gave me", a natural way of saying "my Father's commandments" that makes clear these are commands given to the Son.

decisions.choice: permanecerán ... permanezco
decisions.reason: The same verb for the disciples and for Jesus (meaning decision m3). "Mandamientos" (L, B) and "mandatos" (R), as in 14:15.

source.text: ταῦτα λελάληκα ὑμῖν ἵνα ἡ χαρὰ ἡ ἐμὴ ἐν ὑμῖν ᾖ καὶ ἡ χαρὰ ὑμῶν πληρωθῇ.

records.literal_gloss: These things I have spoken to you so that the joy the mine in you may be and the joy of you may be made full.

en.L: These things I have spoken to you so that the joy that is {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}} may be in you, and your joy may be made full.
en.B: I have said this to you so that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} joy will be in you and your joy will be complete.
en.R: I have told you these things so that you will have {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} joy in you, and so that your joy will be full.

fr.L: Ces choses, je vous les ai dites afin que la joie qui est la {{deity_pronoun:mienne|Mienne}} soit en vous et que votre joie soit rendue pleine.

fr.R: Je vous ai dit ces choses pour que vous ayez {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} joie en vous, et pour que votre joie soit pleine.

sw.L: Mambo haya nimewaambia ili furaha iliyo {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} iwe ndani yenu, na furaha yenu ijazwe kikamilifu.

sw.R: Nimewaambia mambo haya ili mpate kuwa na furaha {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} ndani yenu, na ili furaha yenu ijae.

decisions.choice: may be in you, as the SBLGNT reads
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads ᾖ, "may be". Many later manuscripts read instead "may remain", the verb that runs through 15:4-10. The older witnesses support "may be". A reviewer should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: my joy ... your joy made full: Jesus shares his own joy with them, and it makes theirs complete
decisions.reason: "My joy" is the joy Jesus has in his union with the Father and in doing his will. He speaks so that the same joy may be in the disciples. "Made full" (πληρωθῇ) means complete, lacking nothing; John the Baptist used the same words of his own joy (3:29), and they return in 16:24 and 17:13. This joy comes on the night before Jesus dies, and it is not taken away by grief (16:20-22).

decisions.choice: these things I have spoken: all that Jesus has said about the vine and remaining in him
decisions.reason: "These things" gathers up what he has just said (15:1-10). The phrase recurs through the farewell discourse (14:25; 16:1, 4, 33), each time giving the reason for his words.

decisions.choice: made full (L); complete (B); full (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the passive "made full". Balanced says "complete" and Readable says "full", both plain words for joy that lacks nothing. "Joy" is the key term at every level.

decisions.choice: gozo; sea completo
decisions.reason: Jesus's own joy, shared and made full (meaning decision m2). "Gozo" is the deeper word; "alegría" would also do.
